quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You see a green traffic light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter the intersection until you can completely cross it.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can completely cross it.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can completely cross before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Slow down in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block traffic, you can be ticketed.

questions.question: When daylight is fading, what should you use so others can see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades. Use high beam headlights only in open areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means passing is allowed. A solid yellow line means passing is not allowed. When these lines are next to each other, passing is only allowed from the broken line side.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you can proceed in the arrow's direction if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If a green arrow appears above your lane, you may go in that direction when the road is clear. This applies whether the arrow is alone or with other signals.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car ahead of you.
Drive carefully through the zone without slowing down to look.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the zone without slowing down to look.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things in a construction zone. This causes traffic congestion and is called "rubbernecking."

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward where you want to move.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward where you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Look several times if needed. Watch the traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: Your vehicle wheels leave the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel tight, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake. Once your speed drops, check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter other lanes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in your blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC number means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on ice and snow locks the front brakes, causing you to lose steering control. Drive at an appropriate speed to avoid heavy braking.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
All have air brakes that stop quickly.
They are easier to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks stop more slowly than cars. At 55 mph, a passenger vehicle stops in about 400 feet, but a large truck needs about 800 feet.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Hide in the truck's blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hide in the truck's blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks or buses where cars disappear in the blind spots. "No zones" are also areas where cars are so close to a truck or bus that the driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see the road better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Your tires do not grip gravel and dirt roads as well as concrete or asphalt. When driving on gravel or dirt, slow down. It takes much longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When traffic permits, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Get shorter as vehicle speed increases.
Are not affected by vehicle speed.
Get longer as vehicle speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get longer as vehicle speed increases.
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, it takes longer to stop and crashes are worse.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Get shorter as vehicle speed increases.
Are not affected by vehicle speed.
Get longer as vehicle speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get longer as vehicle speed increases.
questions.explanation: High speeds are dangerous. As speed increases, crashes become more severe and the risk of serious injury or death increases. Leave more distance between you and other vehicles as you go faster so you can stop safely.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and go only when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and go only when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and only go after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: This sign shows:

options.text: An intersection.
A road curve.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to what is immediately ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Even if the water looks shallow, it may hide hazards. Turn around and find another route.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring at the road directly ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware. Staring only at the road ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: What should you do at a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive fast through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a broken traffic light, treat it as an all-way stop. Stop completely unless a police officer directs you. Then look and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A downgrade or hill is coming.
Road construction area.
The road will narrow ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A downgrade or hill is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep or long hill ahead. The hill may have sharp curves.
